column1: # Phase 1 tensor-parallel-2 serving test. A PLUMBING test, not a memory-fit test: it
# serves Qwen3-8B on two cards to prove that --nodes=1 --gpus-per-node=<type>:2 gives
# two devices vLLM can form an NCCL tensor-parallel group across.
# Two live findings force the GPU type, both verified 2026-09-06:
# 1. NOT a100-80, though CONTRACT.md line 18 specifies it. Every a100-80 node carries
#    exactly ONE card (sinfo -o "%n %G": 11 nodes, all gpu:a100-80:1), so
#    --gpus-per-node=a100-80:2 is rejected at submit time with "Requested node
#    configuration is not available". Confirmed by job 825233.
# 2. NOT a100-40 either, though its nodes do carry 2. Slurm serves a100-40 as MIG
#    3g.40gb SLICES of an A100 80GB, and MIG instances have no peer-to-peer path, so
#    NCCL cannot build a tensor-parallel group across them. Job 825248 was refused by
#    the device assertion on exactly this.
# h100-96 is served as whole cards, 2 per node, 11 nodes: the only type on this cluster
# that supports tensor parallelism within the account's caps (h200-141 has 4 per node
# but a per-user cap of 1). At 2 x 96 = 192 GB it is also the right replacement serving
# line for the 70B dense subjects, which need about 140 GB in bf16.
# The 70B memory fit is a separate test when the Llama licence lands; this run serves an
# 8B and never claims otherwise.
# MODEL
Qwen/Qwen3-8B
